text: REST APIs are a common way for applications to communicate. When you design one, you should follow some best practices. First, use clear and meaningful endpoints, such as /users or /orders, so developers can easily understand them. Second, always return the correct status codes. For example, use 200 for success and 404 when something is not found. Third, write good documentation so others know how to use your API. Finally, use versioning, like /v1/users, to keep old and new versions working. These simple rules make your API easier to use and maintain.
